description: Module-level functions for starting the bot, playing games from code and reading its data files.

functions.name: run

params.name: bot
params.description: The bot class, or a factory where the language has no class objects (C++: template argument).

params.name: viewer
params.description: true opens the viewer window for the game (E106, E108); default false.

functions.description: Entry point and the only call in the bot's main. Creates one bot instance, speaks the protocol and returns when the game is over. Transport and log level come from command-line arguments or environment, so the same file runs locally, in a debugger and on the server (E61): --tcp [PORT] connects to 127.0.0.1 (default port 7470) instead of using stdin/stdout, --log-level LEVEL sets the start level (trace, debug, info, warn, error, off), --log-file PATH also writes the log to a file. The environment variables SBM_TRANSPORT (stdio or tcp), SBM_PORT, SBM_LOG_LEVEL and SBM_LOG_FILE do the same; arguments win. Without either the bot uses stdio and INFO. --remote URL plays against a bot on the server at URL instead (E116): with an API token of a coder from --token or, better, SBM_TOKEN, the opponent's name from --opponent, the own color from --color (white, black or random, the default) and either a discipline by name from --discipline or free times from --time SECONDS+INCREMENT (default 60+1); SBM_TRANSPORT=remote with SBM_REMOTE_URL, SBM_OPPONENT, SBM_COLOR, SBM_DISCIPLINE and SBM_TIME do the same. The SDK asks the web API for the game, joins its seat over WebSocket and then speaks the same protocol; the clock runs on the server and includes the network's delay. Other arguments are left to the bot. With viewer the SDK starts the viewer program shipped with it and shows the game in its window, live and step by step; when the game is over the program waits until the window is closed. The viewer stays shut if the environment variable SBM_NO_VIEWER is set to a non-empty value (the sandbox on the server sets it) or the SDK has no viewer program; the latter is logged once at WARN.

functions.name: play

params.name: bot
params.description: The own bot class (C++: template argument); it runs inside the calling program, so a debugger stops at its breakpoints.

params.name: opponent
params.description: Without server: a reference bot (random, material), a bot file or a command as in the local arena (E67). With server: the name of a checked bot on the server.

params.name: server
params.description: Address of the site, e.g. https://schachbotmanager.example.org; absent or empty plays locally (default).

params.name: token
params.description: API token of a coder, needed with server; absent or empty takes SBM_TOKEN from the environment.

params.name: color
params.description: Own color in the first game: white, black or random (default); later games alternate.

params.name: time
params.description: Time control SECONDS+INCREMENT, default 60+1; not together with discipline.

params.name: discipline
params.description: With server only: a discipline by name instead of time.

params.name: viewer
params.description: true opens one viewer window for all games, as with run (E108); default false.

returns.description: One entry per game in the order played.

functions.description: Plays games from code, so a starter script needs neither arguments nor environment variables (E120). Without server the games run in the local arena: the referee in the calling program, the own bot in a thread of it, the opponent as its own process with its log hidden. With server each game is asked for at the web API and played over WebSocket as with --remote of run (E116); the server allows one running game per token, so play waits briefly for the previous one to end. Each result is logged at INFO, the score after the last game. Arguments outside their ranges raise InvalidArgument; an exception of the bot, a refused game or a lost connection is logged at ERROR and ends the process with exit code 1, as with run. With viewer the window shows every game; after the last one the program waits until it is closed.

functions.name: load_data

params.name: name
params.description: File name without directory, as uploaded.

functions.description: Reads a data file uploaded with the bot (E30); the only way to read files. It reads from the directory named by the environment variable SBM_DATA_DIR, which the server sets; without it from the directory data next to the bot's main file (E62). Names that are empty, contain / or \ or are equal to . or .. are invalid.
